metadata.purpose: Candidate chest positions on the Limveld map family.
metadata.space: 1000x1000, top-left origin, same space as mapCoordinates.ts
metadata.source: Detected from design/Chests/chests.webp, authored by Artimuz.
metadata.excluded: Great Hollow has no chest layer.
metadata.note: Position is fixed. Which seed carries a chest lives in the assignments file.
metadata.greatHollow: Great Hollow has its own twelve chest positions, read from greatHollowChests.png.

metadata.purpose: Which chest positions are occupied on each seed.
metadata.method: Per map type and position, the median patch across seeds is the background, because the base map does not change. A chest is a large deviation from it. The strongest deviation in the combo is the chest exemplar, and every seed is scored by shape correlation against it, then split at the widest gap. A combo whose largest deviation stays under the absent ceiling is recorded as never carrying a chest.
metadata.absent: A position missing from a seed entry means no chest there.
metadata.generated: Written by scripts/detect_chests.py. Regenerate rather than hand-editing.

metadata.purpose: Field boss icon positions per map type, bound to the spreadsheet slot names.
metadata.binding: Normal is bound from seed 000, whose twelve icons and names were verified one by one against the source image. The other Limveld maps inherit a slot when a position sits on the same Limveld coordinate. A position with slot null is created by the Shifting Earth and is not in the spreadsheet.
metadata.unbound: A position with slot null is a fixed regional boss, absent from the spreadsheet.
metadata.filter: Positions falling outside the base map landmass are discarded as detection artefacts.
metadata.fixedBoss: Name of a boss created by the Shifting Earth. Constant across every seed of that map type, so it is absent from the spreadsheet and was read from the median image, where fixed labels stay sharp while per-seed labels blur away.
metadata.rottedWoods: Bound by presence: a Rotted Woods slot holding Putrid Ancestral Followers means nothing is drawn at that position in that seed, so each slot has its own pattern of empty seeds. Matching observed presence against that pattern across all fifty Rotted seeds fixes the pairing. Icon type carries no signal here because nearly every boss uses the great icon.
metadata.rottedWoodsNortheast: Far Northeast (779.5,554.5) and Northeast (764,600.5) are two distinct nearby positions. The median only revealed the first because the second is occupied less often; it was read from seed 030.
metadata.greatHollow: Rebuilt from the numbered positions Artimuz authored on GreatHollow.jpg and GreatHollow2.png, not from the median of the old maps. The number to slot mapping comes from row 1 of the Great Hollow sheet.
metadata.greatHollowCastles: Northwest Castle and Southeast Castle hold the castle variant, not a boss name, so they are not field boss positions. Northwest Castle Basement does hold a boss and stays at position 2.

metadata.purpose: Field boss and castle boss identity per named slot, per seed.
metadata.source: Nightreign seed finder Raw Data.xlsx, the original spreadsheet behind the project data.
metadata.slots: Slot names are the spreadsheet's own location labels, not coordinates.
metadata.note: Coordinates are resolved separately by matching these presence patterns against the rendered maps.
metadata.generated: Written by scripts/extract_field_bosses.py. Regenerate rather than hand-editing.

metadata.purpose: Which map icon each boss uses: the blue field icon or the red great icon.
metadata.source: Observed across the rendered maps, then cross-checked against the spreadsheet.
metadata.castle: Castle slots do not follow the boss rule: rooftop is always great, basement always field.
metadata.notFieldBosses: Names the spreadsheet carries in a field boss column that are not field bosses. Confirmed as a spreadsheet error by Artimuz. The extraction keeps them so it stays faithful to the source; the render skips them entirely, icon and label.
metadata.nameAliases: Spelling variants seen in the spreadsheet mapped to the canonical name in reference/bosses.json. Derived by normalising against that roster, plus Golden Hippo, which the roster spells in full. Golden Hippo appears only on DLC seed ids and Golden Hippopotamus only on base ids, so they are the same boss written differently per sheet. Origin of the question: intern_legacy interns/intern_FIELD_BOSSES_TRIAGEM.md.
metadata.outsideRoster: Names with no entry in reference/bosses.json. They render from the observed icon type and still need a ruling from Artimuz.
metadata.greatHollow: The Great Hollow bosses have no counterpart in the Limveld roster and their icon type could not be settled by measurement: their icons are constant across every seed of that map, so a residual against the median vanishes, and template matching on the underground art was inconclusive. Artimuz ruled them all field.

metadata.purpose: Rot Blessing marker, exclusive to the Rotted Woods shifting earth.
metadata.source: Position read from seeds 030, 031 and 032, one per value. The value per seed comes from the Rot Blessing column of the spreadsheet, which the DLC tab does not carry; those ten seeds were read off the rendered maps instead, by correlating the residual against the median at each of the three positions with a canonical example of that position. The method reproduces all forty spreadsheet values before being trusted for the ten it fills in.

metadata.purpose: Short label for each POI slot, per seed.
metadata.source: Major Base and Minor Base columns of Nightreign seed finder Raw Data.xlsx.
metadata.rule: The spreadsheet writes 'Structure - Detail'. Only the detail is kept, which is what the rendered maps already show. A plain church produces no label: the base sheet writes it 'Church - Normal' and the DLC sheet writes bare 'Church'. The DLC also writes 'Town' where the base sheet writes 'Township - Township', so it is normalised to Township.
metadata.slots: Keys are the building slot ids of mapCoordinates.ts, taken from row 1 of the sheet.
metadata.wording: The base game wording is canonical. Where the DLC sheet names the same POI differently it is aligned to the base game, which is why 'Crystalian Alliance' is written 'Crystalians'. Marsh and Forge are DLC-exclusive and have no base-game counterpart, so their wording stands. The DLC sheet also swaps Fire Monk and Mausoleum Knight between the two Great Church variants; the icons are right and the wording is corrected against them.
metadata.labelImpliedByIcon: Slot icons that carry one and only one label across every seed, so the icon alone already tells an experienced player what is there. The map filter uses this to drop those labels in its Minimal mode. Excluded from the list: the empty icon, because a marker with no icon is nothing but its label; the '@event' sentinel, which belongs to another filter group; and Caravans, which the map draws no icon for.
metadata.greatHollow: Not covered. That sheet names its POI columns by location and carries no slot number, so there is no mapping to the twenty Great Hollow slots yet.
metadata.generated: Written by scripts/extract_poi_labels.py. Regenerate rather than hand-editing.

metadata.purpose: Evergaol boss per slot, per seed.
metadata.source: Evergaol columns of Nightreign seed finder Raw Data.xlsx.
metadata.slots: EG1 to EG7, the ids of EVERGAOL_COORDINATES in mapCoordinates.ts. The base sheet names them by id and the DLC sheet by location; both are mapped to the same ids here.
metadata.shiftingEarth: A slot missing for a map type was swallowed by that Shifting Earth. The count per map type is derived from the data, not assumed.
metadata.names: The DLC sheet writes Sword and Spear Crucible Knight where the base sheet writes Crucible Knight with Sword and with Spear. The two spellings never overlap by seed id, so they are the same boss and are normalised to the base spelling.
metadata.greatHollow: Not covered; that map has no Limveld evergaols.
metadata.generated: Written by scripts/extract_evergaols.py. Regenerate rather than hand-editing.

metadata.purpose: The thirty numbered positions of the Great Hollow, read from GreatHollow.jpg.
metadata.space: 1000x1000, top-left origin, same space as mapCoordinates.ts
metadata.source: Numbers authored by Artimuz on GreatHollow.jpg and GreatHollow2.png; badge centres detected and verified against newBlankMaps/GreatHollow_new.webp.
metadata.pending: The Town Merchant has four possible spots that still need reading off the old maps.
metadata.southeastCastle: 31 is the POI, 32 the boss above it and 33 the boss below, which the vertical order of the badges confirms. Holy puts a Divine Beast Warrior in both; Rot puts a Putrid Avatar above and Cleanrot Knights below.
metadata.southGreatChurch: Position 34 is where the Inquisitor sits when the South Great Church takes its Holy form. The Ghostflame Dragon form uses 14 instead.

metadata.purpose: Great Hollow bosses that the Limveld model does not cover, keyed by the numbered position.
metadata.poi: The first number of a grouped column is the POI and is already drawn from seed_data's building slots, so only the bosses appear here.
metadata.kinds: boss draws the boss icon with a label; stack draws three stacked labels and no icon; label draws only text, used by the Sorcerer's Rise secrets whose tower icon already comes from seed_data. Secrets use the spelling written on the rendered maps.
metadata.holyChurch: When the South Great Church takes its Holy form, the Inquisitor stands at 34 rather than 14, which is where the Ghostflame Dragon form puts its first boss.
metadata.order: Within a grouped cell the bosses follow the order written in the sheet, mapped to the positions after the POI. West Ruin is the exception: its two are written in the reverse order of the map, checked against the rendered maps, so they are swapped on extraction.
metadata.castles: Northwest Castle and Southeast Castle cells hold the variant, not a boss. Godskins puts a Godskin Duo at 1 and Fire Knights a Golden Hippopotamus. Hornsent puts a Divine Beast Warrior at both 32 and 33; Cleanrot Knights puts a Putrid Avatar at 32 and Cleanrot Knights at 33.
metadata.generated: Written by scripts/extract_great_hollow.py. Regenerate rather than hand-editing.

metadata.purpose: Town Merchant of the Great Hollow: four possible spots and which one each seed uses.
metadata.source: Spots mapped by Artimuz on GH_merchant_coords.png. The two underground ones were transposed to the new base map, which places that piece differently; the transposed coordinates are the ones stored here. Each spot was matched to its spreadsheet name by finding the merchant in a seed carrying that value.

metadata.purpose: Which Great Hollow seeds spawn the Legendary Merchant on Day 2.
metadata.source: Seed list supplied by Artimuz. Wording and placement follow the reference render ex1007.png, which prints the note above the landmass rather than at a map location.
metadata.position: A single caption slot shared by every seed in the list. It is a note, not a location: the merchant's spawn point is not recorded.
metadata.label: Rendered as text only, in the same event style as the Day 2 Circle note.

metadata.purpose: Where the Day 2 Circle marker sits on the Great Hollow, per seed.
metadata.source: The two spots come from Day_2_Circle.png. Which one a seed uses was read from the rendered maps by finding the red diamond; the sheet does not carry it, since its Night 2 Circle column is Divine Tower on every seed.
metadata.label: Rendered as text only, in the same style as the Limveld map events.

metadata.purpose: Where each night circle closes, and which boss waits there, per seed.
metadata.source: Names and bosses come from the Night 1 and Night 2 columns of the spreadsheet.
metadata.positions: Found on the rendered maps: for each name the mean blue tint of the seeds carrying it is contrasted against the seeds that do not, which leaves only that circle, and the peak of the contrast is its centre. Every centre within 12 units of a point marked by hand in nightbosses_coord/ is snapped to that point. A name shared by several map types is averaged across them; they agree to within a few units.
metadata.shiftingEarth: On a Shifting Earth map night 2 always closes inside the Shifting Earth, so those names belong to that map type alone.
metadata.label: Rendered as 1. <boss> and 2. <boss>, matching the old maps.
metadata.generated: Positions by scripts/locate_night_circles.py, this file by scripts/build_night_circles.py. Regenerate rather than hand-editing.

metadata.purpose: Which faction garrisons the Limveld castle, per seed, as a label with no icon.
metadata.position: One point, marked by hand in Castle_crew.png. It sits just above the two castle boss icons, which is where the rendered maps put this label.
metadata.source: The Castle column of Nightreign seed finder Raw Data.xlsx.
metadata.appliesTo: Derived from the data, not assumed. Noklateo swallows the castle and leaves the column empty on all fifty of its seeds. The Great Hollow castle follows a different structure and is not covered by this sheet.
metadata.notBosses: Trolls, Crucible Knights and Banished Knights garrison the castle; none of the three is a field boss, so they never appear in the field boss layer.
metadata.generated: Written by scripts/extract_castle_crew.py. Regenerate rather than hand-editing.

bossCatalog.name: Ancestor Spirit
bossCatalog.summary: A spectral deer. The antler sweep covers a wide arc to either side, so the space beside it is the dangerous place to stand, but the windup is slow enough to read.

bossCatalog.name: Ancient Dragon
bossCatalog.summary: Several of its attacks are AoE and can wipe a team in a couple of exchanges. Below 75% health red lightning starts running through its body, adding a lightning follow-up to most of them. Pierce works, the head takes double, and stance breaking does not.

bossCatalog.name: Ancient Hero of Zamor
bossCatalog.summary: Around 60% health it drops to its knees and channels frost into the sword, and from then on its strikes build frostbite. Before that it is a fast swordfighter with repeating windups, so the speed is the problem rather than the reading. Fire and lightning both work well.

bossCatalog.name: Artorias
bossCatalog.summary: Hard to read, with only small tells before each attack. Holding about twice his reach of distance works even for melee, and rolling out is more reliable than trading.

bossCatalog.name: Battlefield Commander
bossCatalog.summary: Tanky and hard to stagger, but slow. He summons Exile Soldiers, and the summon animation is the longest opening you get. He will call more later, so clearing the first wave does not end it.

bossCatalog.name: Bell Bearing Hunter
bossCatalog.summary: Pierce roughly doubles on it and lightning lands well, while standard, slash and strike are all resisted. It is aggressive at close and mid range but the attacks are slow, and it can be parried, though a stance break costs two parries rather than one.

bossCatalog.name: Black Blade Kindred
bossCatalog.summary: Most of what it does is slow and well signposted. The exception is Fury of the Kindred, a five-hit combo with awkward gaps between the slashes; when the sword comes up to the left of its face, sprint out rather than roll.

bossCatalog.name: Black Knife Assassin
bossCatalog.summary: The feint is what gets people: she leaps in with a counterclockwise slash that is not real, then follows with the clockwise one that is. Most physical damage lands, pierce least of all. Let her come to you rather than chasing.

bossCatalog.name: Centipede Demon
bossCatalog.summary: The tail can be cut off, which helps, but the severed piece keeps attacking until you kill it and the tail eventually grows back. No lava pool here, unlike its Dark Souls original.

bossCatalog.name: Crucible Knight & Golden Hippopotamus
bossCatalog.summary: Starts as a one-on-one against the Crucible Knight. Below half health he raises a knee and stomps out a burst of holy energy, which is when the Golden Hippopotamus arrives. Fire and lightning hurt both of them, and the hippo takes slash on top.

bossCatalog.name: Dancer of the Boreal Valley
bossCatalog.summary: Her reach is longer than it looks, which is what catches people out. Phase one opens calm with a single sword and gets more aggressive as her health drops.

bossCatalog.name: Dancing Lion
bossCatalog.summary: It cycles through lightning, frost and wind on a rotation rather than at health thresholds, keeping its base moveset and adding a few attacks with each form. Faster than its size suggests, and some of its attacks make a mess of the camera.

bossCatalog.name: Divine Beast Warrior & Curseblade
bossCatalog.summary: Both spawn together, and the Curseblade opens by impairing your vision while the Divine Beast Warrior slams down lightning. Kill the Curseblade first: it is the weaker of the two, and the curse goes with it.

bossCatalog.name: Death Knights
bossCatalog.summary: One Twin Axe knight first, then three more together: two with Longhaft Axes and one with Twin Axes. The moveset is not the problem, the number is. Split them up and take them one each.

bossCatalog.name: Death Rite Bird
bossCatalog.summary: Most of its attacks are slow enough to read, but it leaps and flies to reposition constantly, so a fair part of the fight is spent chasing it. Back off for the ghostflame.

bossCatalog.name: Demi-Human Queen
bossCatalog.summary: Her poise is low, so stance breaks come quickly. The opener is usually a staff slam into a sideways drag along the ground, and getting through both buys you a pause. Fire, poison and scarlet rot all work; madness does nothing.

bossCatalog.name: Demi-Human Queen & Swordmaster
bossCatalog.summary: Both at once. The Swordmaster darts around but has low poise, so steady pressure keeps him staggered. The Queen opens slow and telegraphed, then drops her staff partway through and goes feral on all fours, with faster claw swipes and a jaw snap.

bossCatalog.name: Demon Prince
bossCatalog.summary: Which version you fight depends on which Day 1 demon died last. The Demon in Pain gives a black-red variant with meteorites and the widest damage windows; the Demon from Below gives an orange one with lasers and an aerial sweep.

bossCatalog.name: Demon in Pain & Demon from Below
bossCatalog.summary: You fight both at once: the Demon in Pain in darker red, the Demon from Below in lighter orange. They sweep poison breath in wide arcs and slam the ground for fire explosions, and neither can be poisoned or frostbitten. Slash and blood loss work.

bossCatalog.name: Draconic Tree Sentinel
bossCatalog.summary: A golden-armored knight on horseback with lightning and fireballs at every range. The raised shield means a single-target bolt; the hammer planted behind him means a wide wave. Poison and Scarlet Rot work unusually well.

bossCatalog.name: Draconic Tree Sentinel and Royal Cavalrymen
Dragonkin Soldier
bossCatalog.summary: Slow, but with long reach and delayed swings that punish an early roll; wait the delay out and there is room to close in afterwards. Slash gets through at full damage where lightning barely does, and a stance break gives you a critical.

bossCatalog.name: The Duke's Dear Freja
bossCatalog.summary: A two-headed spider armored everywhere but the heads, so those are the only targets that count. The smaller spiders she summons web you down and knock you over, and that is usually what kills people rather than Freja.

bossCatalog.name: Elder Lion
bossCatalog.summary: A chained beast with a sword fused into one arm. It is faster than something that size should be and its hits can break a guard, but the big swings leave room to answer.

bossCatalog.name: Erdtree Avatar
bossCatalog.summary: It deals Holy damage and resists Holy, so a holy loadout is the wrong answer twice over; fire does roughly double. A headless stump with a huge staff, slow and easy to read, but the leaping body slam sends out a shockwave when it lands.

bossCatalog.name: Fallingstar Beast
bossCatalog.summary: Magic, fire, lightning and holy all get through, so bring whatever you have. Most of what it does travels in a straight line, so strafe rather than roll, and the recovery after each attack is long. It still crosses the arena faster than its size suggests.

bossCatalog.name: Flying Dragon
bossCatalog.summary: It does not lean on fire the way other dragons do, and every move has a clear cue. Pierce is what works, the head takes extra, and the bite is a feint: it turns its head one way, roars, then snaps from the other side.

bossCatalog.name: Gaping Dragon
bossCatalog.summary: One of the easier ones. Cut the tail off early. It drops loot and it shortens the tail sweep, which otherwise reaches further than it looks like it should. The ribcage slam leaves it stunned afterwards, and lightning gets through better than anything else if you have it.

bossCatalog.name: Godskin Duo
bossCatalog.summary: The Apostle uses a twinblade and a sickle that yanks you into close range; the Noble thrusts and answers distance with Black Flame. Separate health bars, unlike Elden Ring, and the survivor will not bring the other back.

bossCatalog.name: Golden Hippopotamus
bossCatalog.summary: It pauses after each attack, and those pauses are where the fight is won. The jaws-open charge is the dangerous one: it grabs you and slams you repeatedly, and the lunging bite reaches further than the animation suggests. Fire and lightning both do double.

bossCatalog.name: Grafted Monarch
bossCatalog.summary: When he swings the axe into a cyclone around himself, stop using ranged attacks, because it reflects projectiles. He can be stance-broken for a critical, and if you press him hard he grows a thorned tail and sweeps with it.

bossCatalog.name: Grafted Scion
bossCatalog.summary: Fast swordwork from one or two blades at once, coming from angles that change each time, with sudden area attacks mixed in. The pause at the end of a combo is your window.

bossCatalog.name: Great Red Bear
bossCatalog.summary: Big and slow, with everything telegraphed. It roars before it starts, which is free damage, and after that it is a close-range fight with a few AoE swings to step out of.

bossCatalog.name: Great Wyrm
bossCatalog.summary: Carries a giant scalesword and spits magma that stays on the ground and keeps burning. The head takes the most damage and can be staggered, but the head is also the part that never stops moving.

bossCatalog.name: Leonine Misbegotten
bossCatalog.summary: A greatsword swung with more strength than technique, fast and heavy, but the bigger attacks leave openings wide enough that patience beats trading. Watch the stomp, which rolls straight into a spin and a half with the blade out. Slash and fire both work.

bossCatalog.name: Magma Wyrm
bossCatalog.summary: Fire is close to useless here, which catches people out on a boss that spits lava. Physical damage works instead, and the head takes extra. Molten breath and the scalesword cover a lot of ground between them, and a confined arena makes that worse.

bossCatalog.name: Miranda Blossom
bossCatalog.summary: It does not move, which makes it easy to leave alone. When the petals close it is about to release pollen across a wide radius that builds poison fast, so back out and come back once it clears.

bossCatalog.name: Mohg
bossCatalog.summary: The Lord of Blood hits hard and builds Blood Loss, but he is slow enough to punish. Most of what he does covers a wide area, so mid range is the safer place to stand.

bossCatalog.name: Morgott
bossCatalog.summary: Long combos with delayed wind-ups, which is what breaks people's dodge and parry timing, and parrying is expensive at three per stance break. He throws spectral daggers, rains spectral swords across a wide area, and erupts into flame at close range. Slash is the answer.

bossCatalog.name: Nameless King
bossCatalog.summary: The two phases want opposite damage. Mounted on the storm drake he takes lightning; on foot he resists it heavily and takes holy instead. Lightning is coming at you either way, so bring resistance, and the drake is big enough to give the camera trouble.

bossCatalog.name: Night's Cavalry
bossCatalog.summary: Getting it off the horse is most of the fight; on foot it loses the charge and the repositioning. It still swings wide, and the hilt slam puts out a shockwave that knocks back everyone inside the circle.

bossCatalog.name: Night's Cavalry Duo
bossCatalog.summary: Two of them, one with a glaive and one with a flail. Whichever one nobody is holding will be free to hit whoever is busy, so the team has to split.

bossCatalog.name: Outland Commander
bossCatalog.summary: It opens by summoning two spectral Banished Knights, and that animation is a free window. The Knights hit harder than he does, and he is slow and hard to stagger, so they are the first problem.

bossCatalog.name: Red Wolf
bossCatalog.summary: A giant wolf that casts. It alternates between closing for bites and throwing sorcery from across the arena, and the one to watch is the glintblade: it sidesteps, leaves a floating orb behind, and the orb fires at you a moment later, homing.

bossCatalog.name: Royal Carian Knight
bossCatalog.summary: Breaking its stance or parrying it only stuns it for a moment, with no critical at the end, which makes it unusual. Armored knight and armored horse together, glintstone sorcery mixed into the melee, and lightning is the damage type that passes through cleanly.

bossCatalog.name: Royal Revenant
bossCatalog.summary: Cast a healing incantation near it and the cast itself damages and stuns it. Part human, part spider, which is what makes its movements hard to read, but the flurries leave clear gaps, slash cuts through it, and holy does not.

bossCatalog.name: Smelter Demon
bossCatalog.summary: Slow and linear, and one of the more forgiving fights you will get. The exception is the lunge into a sword thrust, which closes distance faster than the rest of his moveset suggests.

bossCatalog.name: Tibia Mariner
bossCatalog.summary: A skeleton on a ghost boat, blowing a horn to raise more skeletons. It is slow itself, but it teleports away and keeps summoning, so the fight drags if the adds pile up.

bossCatalog.name: Tree Sentinel
bossCatalog.summary: Heavily armored and mounted, with a halberd that reaches further than you want it to, and a horse that hits you as well. It takes full damage from lightning and shrugs off fire and holy.

bossCatalog.name: Ulcerated Tree Spirit
bossCatalog.summary: The whole fight is learning which of its movements actually have a hitbox. It flops and twists constantly and most of that is harmless, which makes the real attacks easy to miss.

bossCatalog.name: Valiant Gargoyle
bossCatalog.summary: Stone, and much quicker than stone should be. It carries a sword and a halberd and swaps between them mid-fight.

bossCatalog.name: Wormface
bossCatalog.summary: A cloaked figure with a head of writhing worms. The head smash telegraphs itself completely, but it often follows into a second slam or a sweep, so take your two hits and get out.
